label: Evals become the spec
title: What you write down stops being the code
thesis: As machines write more of the implementation, the artifact that defines what "done" means shifts from the code and the product document toward an executable evaluation suite. Teams increasingly specify behaviour as acceptance criteria a machine can run, and the eval set rather than the source becomes the thing under deliberate human authorship.
currentPressure: Generated implementations vary between runs and between models, so reading the code no longer tells a team whether the intended behaviour holds.

implications.statement: Writing precise, falsifiable acceptance criteria becomes a more valuable skill than writing the implementation it constrains.
The durable artifact a team maintains shifts from source code towards the evaluation suite that bounds it.
Sign-off moves from reviewing a change to accepting the evidence that a change satisfies its stated criteria.

evidence.note: eval suites treated as the primary artifact; an 'evals engineer' role appearing in postings
structured pre-change impact analysis cuts agent regressions 70% — designed verification works where naive instruction does not
the verification gap: 96% do not fully trust generated code, under half always verify
newer models pass more checkpoints while emitting more unrequested change — pressure for tighter criteria
agent-generated tests provide only marginal utility, undercutting the labour saving the practice depends on

The author states his credence in agent output turns on the presence of conformance suites, tests and reproducible instructions rather than on reading the code. Secondary: a roundup reporting Cursor's planner/worker/judge experiments rather than its own observation.

reachRationale: Named practitioner teams are treating eval suites as their primary specification and a dedicated role is appearing in job postings, but the practice is confined to teams building AI features and has not reached mainstream delivery.
whatWouldChangeThis: Eval suites stay confined to AI-feature teams through 2027 while mainstream delivery remains document- and code-centric
Machine-generated evaluations prove no more trustworthy than machine-generated tests, removing the labour saving that makes the practice attractive

developmentPaths.title: Evals as the primary artifact
developmentPaths.description: The evaluation suite becomes the reviewed, versioned specification; code is treated as generated output.

developmentPaths.title: Evals as a gate, not a spec
developmentPaths.description: Eval suites are adopted purely as a release gate while intent continues to live in prose and code.

developmentPaths.title: Specification stays prose
developmentPaths.description: Executable criteria prove too costly to author and maintain, and specification remains a human-to-human document.
